set.body:
The two concrete API changes ranked #1 and #2 by the API reviewer. I filed the tiering and error-message changes and never filed these, which are the only ones that change the call count.

CHANGE 1 - accept a frame spec for at=, derive the domain. 7 calls becomes 6. Pure ceremony, no semantic content.
  Today the user must build the frame separately and pass the IDENTICAL domain object, which the package then CHECKS they did. Inside plan_geometry, geometry and plan_crossnobis: if at inherits the frame-spec class, compile it against the relation domain. The domain-identity check SURVIVES AND IMPROVES - the frame is compiled against the relation own domain, which removes the mismatch failure mode entirely rather than detecting it after the fact.

CHANGE 2 - let rsa, rdm, contrast and crossnobis accept a relation directly. 6 calls becomes 5, in 2 statements.
  This is SAFE, and the mechanism already exists: R/views.R:269-273 shows these verbs already branch on plan-versus-form and go query-first when handed a plan. The wrapper builds a plan and delegates to that branch. It never calls geometry. It never accepts block storage. It returns the same view class with the same query-only completeness marker it returns today.

  EXCLUDE geometry_spectrum. It requires a complete form (R/views.R:319) and would have to materialize, which is a hidden allocation decision. Let it keep failing with a message naming geometry(plan) as the fix.

RESULT: 5 calls in 2 statements against rMVPA 6 statements. Competitive, with every guarantee intact.

WHY IT CANNOT GO BELOW 5, and this is the part to preserve: over= must stay required. cross_partitions hard-codes independence to independent (R/pairing.R:108 to :17), which sets the estimate attribute to cross_generalized (R/pairing.R:83). That is a claim about the USER data - that run estimates are statistically independent - and it is false if runs share nuisance regressors or came from one GLM across all runs. R/pairing.R:50-53 forces the opposite for self-pairs precisely to stop anything asserting this silently. A true one-liner would assert run independence on the user behalf and must not be built.

MIDDLE PATH worth considering: accept a small enumerated vocabulary for over, so the user types the claim without needing the word pairing. The claim stays explicit; only the noun goes away.
set.title: Shorten the path to 5 calls: accept a frame spec for at=, and let the fixed-query verbs accept a relation
